name: Galgar
summary: Near the Den in the Valley of Trials, Galgar feeds young recruits serving the Horde. He asks newcomers to gather wild cactus apples for his Cactus Apple Surprise.

sections.title: A Cook in the Valley
sections.body: Galgar cooks near the Den's fire in the Valley of Trials, feeding young orcs and trolls through their first rites of passage. Durotar is a dry, harsh red wasteland, where food must be found across the land. Galgar sends novice warriors to gather ripe cactus fruit, testing their attention and resilience while stocking his kitchen.

sections.title: Cactus Apple Surprise
sections.body: Galgar's specialty is called Cactus Apple Surprise. He says gathering spiny desert fruit is a simple task meant to ease fresh recruits into adventuring. The dish still feeds hungry trainees. Every Horde warrior begins somewhere, and Galgar starts them with foraging in the desert.

faq.answer: Galgar is near the central campfire and cooking area outside the Den, in the Valley of Trials, the starting canyon for orcs and trolls in southwestern Durotar.

faq.q: What does Galgar ask adventurers to do?
faq.answer: Galgar asks new adventurers to gather ripe cactus apples from the wild cacti scattered across the Valley of Trials so he can prepare his Cactus Apple Surprise.

faq.q: Why does Galgar send new recruits to pick fruit?
faq.answer: Galgar says the task is simple, giving fledgling fighters an early chore to learn the valley and practice self-sufficiency in Durotar's harsh wilderness.
Cactus Apple Surprise is Galgar's signature recipe, made with fresh cactus apples gathered from Durotar's native desert plants to feed novice recruits.

angles.text: Galgar cooks in the Horde's practical, rustic way, using Durotar's sparse natural resources to feed recruits and keep them ready for battle.
As a young orc in the Valley of Trials, you run an errand for Galgar as a familiar rite of passage before facing fiercer wilderness threats.
